media:group.media:title: When to use Claude subagents
media:group.media:description:
“When a model prefers its own outputs, it’s going to be more lenient at verifying them.”
From Thariq (Anthropic):
“For example, for ‘Is this a good video short or not?’ you should have a rubric and a separate verification agent that reviews the short to make sure it’s good.
You should have two separate Claudes: one doing the work and one verifying it.”

entry.title: We cut Claude Code's system prompt by 80%

media:group.media:title: We cut Claude Code's system prompt by 80%
media:group.media:description:
“As the models have gotten smarter, they need less direction, fewer constraints, and fewer examples.”
From Thariq (Anthropic):
“The examples are constraining it because now it’s like, ‘Oh, you want things like this example.’ If you remove the examples, it can actually be more free-form.
Oftentimes when you say ‘never,’ you don’t really mean never. You mean, ‘Most of the time, don’t do this.’ If you give it the reason instead, that can be more effective.
All this is to say that you want to trim your context. The latest models often need more room to run.”
📌 Watch the full episode on my YouTube.

entry.title: Planning with Claude is about finding the unknowns

media:group.media:title: Planning with Claude is about finding the unknowns
media:group.media:description:
“I don’t think of speccing as just happening at the start.”
From Thariq (Anthropic):
“I start with a request and then the agent does some exploration. I then do some mockups or explainers to understand my unknowns.
I ask Claude to keep implementation notes so that it finds out what we weren’t expecting. Once we have that, we can respec if we need to.
It’s much less like one handoff from spec to implementation and more of this back-and-forth process.”

entry.title: Codex helps me manage my meetings

media:group.media:title: Codex helps me manage my meetings
media:group.media:description:
Codex isn’t just for shipping code. It can also help protect your calendar.
From Rohan (Codex PM):
“I probably have a pretty large number of meetings relative to what would be optimal, but a lot of that’s actually just with customers.
I would say my build time is from 5 PM onwards.
But it’s funny because I’ll even use Codex as my personal chief of staff.
At the beginning of the week, I’ll have it look at all my meetings, consolidate the ones where it can give me focus blocks, and figure out which ones could be canceled as a DM or something.
So it’s definitely helping me find the focus time. But in general, what we do with the free time is actually just spend way more time with our customers.”

entry.title: Why you're not being ambitious enough with Codex

media:group.media:title: Why you're not being ambitious enough with Codex
media:group.media:description:
“Developers even haven’t fully warmed up to the level of ambition you can have with Codex."
From Rohan (Codex PM):
"If you go into any large enterprise, maybe the top five to ten percent most AI-pilled frontier engineers are maximally leveraging Codex. But then there’s a long tail of people that are still maybe pair programming, doing less delegation.
Engineers have seen AI incrementally expand its capabilities over the last three years. But if you look to a non-developer, it’s kind of been just ChatGPT this whole time.
The type of things they’re asking ChatGPT are very different than what you can actually delegate to Codex.
Almost everything you need to do professionally should almost always just immediately have Codex start doing it.”
